site.name: Black King
site.location: Boulder County Tungsten Mining District / Mammoth-Tungsten Mountain area
overview: Black King was a documented tungsten exploration property in Boulder County's historic tungsten district, developed northeast of the Mammoth shaft to test several veins at depth.
State and federal mining reports describe a long underground tunnel, named ownership and operators, and its relationship to the nearby Mammoth and Tungsten Mountain workings.

timeline.text: Black King was developed as an underground tungsten exploration property in the Boulder County tungsten district.
U.S. Geological Survey reporting documented the Black King tunnel and recorded Gold, Silver & Tungsten, Inc. as the owner at that time.

Colorado's tungsten-mine inventory recorded George Cowdery as owner, Tungsten Mountain Mining Co. as the last operator, no recorded production, and an approximately 1,800-foot tunnel driven to explore several veins.

moreHistory: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 245 places the Black King tunnel about 800 feet northeast of the Mammoth shaft at roughly 8,625 feet elevation. The federal report states that the tunnel was driven to explore several veins at depth and that no production was recorded.

Colorado's Tungsten Mines of Colorado places Black King in the southeast quarter of Section 29, Township 1 South, Range 72 West. It describes an approximately 1,800-foot tunnel and notes potential underground connections toward the Tungsten Mountain No. 9 and Mammoth ore zones.

A mineral-locality record places Black King near 39.935278, -105.472778. This point identifies the documented historic mine locality and does not imply that a surviving portal is open, safe, or publicly accessible today.
